# Coca-Cola (KO) Reverse DCF

A reverse discounted-cash-flow model. Instead of forecasting growth to find a value, it takes
today's **market price**, backs out the constant FCFF growth rate the market is already
discounting for the next 10 years, and tests that growth against Coca-Cola's own history.

* **Python engine** (`src/reverse_dcf/`) — SEC data → FCFF → WACC → solver → sensitivities.
* **Excel model** (`outputs/reverse_dcf_model.xlsx`) — generated by the engine; every number is a
  live formula (the implied growth is solved *inside* Excel), and a `Model Checks` sheet reconciles
  it to the Python results line by line.
* Running the model rewrites `outputs/reverse_dcf_model.xlsx`. The copy in `excel_formatted/` is a snapshot of the same model, formatted and saved in Excel for easy viewing. It is not updated automatically, so after changing inputs, open the new file from `outputs/` in Excel, save it into `excel_formatted/`, and replace the old copy.
* All SEC data comes from the same SEC API as before (`data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts`).

## Quick start

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
export SEC_USER_AGENT="Your Name your.email@example.com"   # only needed to refresh SEC data
python run_model.py                      # Oct-23-2026 snapshot from data/market_inputs.csv
python run_model.py --refresh            # re-download SEC company facts first
python run_model.py --mid-year           # mid-year discounting
python run_model.py --simple-bridge      # EV = mkt cap + debt - cash only (no equity-method adj.)
python run_model.py --valuation-date 2026-10-28 --price <close>   # roll forward to the Q3 10-Q
python -m pytest                         # tests (Excel parity tests need LibreOffice)
```

Units: **USD millions** and **millions of shares** everywhere; rates are decimals.

## Methodology — how the implied growth is backed out

1. **Market EV (target)** = price × diluted shares + debt & operating leases + noncontrolling interests
   − cash, short-term investments & marketable securities − equity-method investments.
   (EBIT excludes equity income, so the investments are non-operating and must come out of EV.)
2. **WACC** = E/(D+E)·[rf + β·ERP] + D/(D+E)·kd·(1−t), market-value weights, marginal tax rate.
3. **Base FCFF₀** (TTM) = EBIT(1 − effective tax rate) + D&A − CapEx − ΔNWC, with TTM =
   last fiscal year + current YTD − prior-year YTD.
4. **Solve** for g such that

   `EV_market = Σₜ₌₁ᴺ FCFF₀(1+g)ᵗ/(1+WACC)ᵗ + FCFF₀(1+g)ᴺ(1+gT)/(WACC−gT)/(1+WACC)ᴺ`

   Because the explicit PV is a geometric series in q = (1+g)/(1+WACC), EV(g) has the closed form
   `(1+WACC)^(m/2)·FCFF₀·[q(1−qᴺ)/(1−q) + qᴺ(1+gT)/(WACC−gT)]` (m = 1 for mid-year). EV is strictly
   increasing in g, so the root is unique. Python uses Brent's method; Excel uses a 60-step
   bisection on the same formula. They agree to ~1e‑16.
5. **Plausibility (Damodaran)** — compare the implied g with (i) revenue and EBIT CAGRs, (ii)
   *fundamental growth* = reinvestment rate × ROIC, and (iii) the year‑10 FCFF margin the implied path
   would require.

### Result — valuation date 23‑Oct‑2026, price $92.71

| | |
|---|---|
| SEC basis (strict as-of) | Q2 2026 10‑Q, TTM to 3‑Jul‑2026 |
| Market EV | $410,093 m |
| WACC | 7.31 % |
| Base FCFF (TTM) | $12,161 m |
| Terminal growth | 2.50 % |
| **Market-implied FCFF growth (10 y)** | **8.25 %** (7.80 % mid-year) |
| Terminal value share of EV | 68.9 % |
| Benchmarks | revenue CAGR 3/5/6y 3.7 / 7.7 / 4.3 %; EBIT CAGR 8.1 / 8.9 / 5.3 %; fundamental growth 1.7 % (ROIC 26.7 % × normalised reinvestment 6.4 %) |

Reading: the price needs FCFF to compound at roughly the *best* recent EBIT growth (a post-COVID,
post-charge rebound) for ten years, far above what reinvestment supports (~1.7 %). Reaching it
requires sustained margin expansion: at 5 % revenue growth the year‑10 FCFF margin must be ~33 %
vs. a NOPAT margin of ~25 % today. The implied rate is a statement about the price, not a forecast.

CC code mis-indented, units mixed ($bn/$m) | Mid-year switch (Excel + Python), requirements, real tests, one unit system |

## Excel layout

`Summary` (KPIs, plausibility table, 3 charts) · `Inputs` · `Historical`· `DCF Engine` · `Sensitivity` ·
`Methodology`. `Model Checks` · `SEC Data` · `Solver` ·  `Solver Grid` ·

Standards: Arial 10, gridlines off, **blue = hard-coded input/historical data, black = formula or link**,
USD millions `#,##0;(#,##0)`, rates `0.00%`, dates `d-mmm-yy`, period headers computed with `EDATE`
from the SEC period end, frozen panes, one-page-wide landscape print setup.

## Project layout

```
coca_cola_reverse_dcf/
│
├── run_model.py                     CLI entry point: runs the model and writes the Excel file
├── requirements.txt                 Python dependencies
├── conftest.py                      lets pytest import the project
├── README.md                        this file
│
├── data/
│   ├── market_inputs.csv            price, rf, ERP, beta, kd, tax, terminal g (non-SEC inputs, with sources)
│   └── raw/                         SEC company facts download (gitignored)
│
├── src/reverse_dcf/                 the Python engine
│   ├── config.py                    inputs, settings, WACC
│   ├── sec.py                       point-in-time XBRL extraction from the SEC API
│   ├── fcff.py                      FCFF calculation (vectorised)
│   ├── dcf.py                       explicit schedule + closed-form EV
│   ├── reverse_dcf.py               Brent and bisection solvers for implied growth
│   ├── sensitivities.py             numpy sensitivity grids
│   ├── fundamentals.py              plausibility metrics (CAGR, ROIC, fundamental growth)
│   ├── model.py                     orchestration: ties all of the above together
│   ├── excel_model.py               workbook builder + LibreOffice recalculation
│   └── outputs.py                   JSON / CSV exports
│
├── excel_formatted/                 formatted model, finished and saved in Excel
│   └── Final_Reverse_DCF_Model.xlsx
│
├── outputs/                         generated each time run_model.py runs
│   └── reverse_dcf_model.xlsx       Excel model generated by the code (other outputs are gitignored)
│
├── scripts/
│   ├── download_sec_data.py         downloads the SEC data
│   └── legacy_html_extraction/      old 10-K / 10-Q HTML scrapers (no longer used by the model)
│
└── tests/                           math, point-in-time (no look-ahead), Excel-vs-Python parity
```

## Limitations

Constant growth then perpetuity (no fade); terminal reinvestment is not re-based to g/ROIC;
regression beta 0.58 is low; equity-method investments and
minority interests at book value; operating leases from the latest 10‑K; TTM ΔNWC includes tax
items and is volatile (see sensitivity above); price, risk-free rate, ERP, beta and cost of debt
are manual inputs — verify them before relying on the output. Not investment advice.
